{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nc-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"f54141a39c5dae89f536a78393eca89e54612a906931304b15934268e0dc7c91","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nc-class-c:lineage:14","source_registry_sha256":"e128656a3d00ba5437556728ebd87f5842c83601163739613417fe77cf9f423b","source_liveness_sha256":"dbfdf3e6d892a41c42c05809a9213d44a78aedd480dc6de23937c97292428b74"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Alcohol, impaired driving and the law","heading":"C — Alcohol and the law: DWI, chemical tests, penalties, BAC restrictions and underage drinking (North Carolina)","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Alcohol and the law: DWI, chemical tests, penalties, BAC restrictions and underage drinking (North Carolina)
Knowledge domain: how alcohol impairs driving, how North Carolina proves and punishes DWI, and the extra rules for underage drivers.

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
At a blood alcohol concentration, or BAC, of 0.08 percent every driver is impaired, and many people are affected at far lower levels. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
Crash risk begins rising at a BAC of 0.05 percent, and at 0.08 percent the chance of causing a fatal crash is greater still. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
The Safe Roads Act of 1983 replaced all earlier North Carolina drunk-driving laws with a single offense called Driving While Impaired, or DWI. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
A driver charged with DWI will be asked to take a chemical test of breath or blood. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A01
Refusing a required chemical test brings an immediate license revocation of at least 30 days and a further DMV revocation of at least 12 months. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A01
In some cases, once six months of a willful-refusal revocation have passed, a judge may grant a limited driving privilege. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A01
A test result of 0.08 or more, or 0.04 or more in a commercial motor vehicle, means your driving privilege is revoked immediately for at least 30 days. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A01
Both your chemical test result and any refusal to be tested can be used as evidence in court. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A01
DWI can be proven by showing that alcohol, drugs or both appreciably impaired the driver's physical or mental faculties. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A01
DWI can also be proven by a BAC of 0.08 percent or more, or 0.04 or more when driving a commercial motor vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A01
North Carolina DWI laws allow law enforcement to set up roadblocks to check for impaired drivers. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A01
Drinking any alcoholic beverage while driving, beer included, is prohibited. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A01
Carrying an open container of any alcoholic beverage in a vehicle, including in the passenger area, is prohibited. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A01
In the passenger area of a commercial motor vehicle on a public road, alcohol is banned whether the container is open or closed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A01
Punishment levels rise with the seriousness of the offense, and a second DWI conviction requires time in jail. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A02
DWI laws aim to help offenders with alcohol problems as well as punish them: repeat offenders and high-BAC drivers are checked for an alcohol problem, and lower-BAC offenders attend alcohol safety school. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A02
Anyone convicted of DWI must complete a substance abuse assessment before driving privileges are reinstated. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A02
A first DWI conviction brings a mandatory one-year license revocation. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A02
A second DWI conviction brings a mandatory four-year revocation when the earlier offense happened within three years of the current one. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A02
A third DWI conviction brings mandatory permanent revocation if at least one earlier conviction happened within the past five years. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A02
A fourth DWI conviction brings mandatory permanent revocation, and it is a felony if the three earlier convictions all happened within the past seven years. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A02
A blood alcohol concentration restriction is placed on a license restored after a DWI suspension, or on a Limited Driving Privilege granted after a DWI conviction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A02
The restriction is 0.04 on the first restoration and 0.00 on the second or any later restoration. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A02
The restriction is also 0.00 after a DWI conviction in a commercial motor vehicle, a conviction for driving under 21 after consuming alcohol or drugs, or felony death by vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A02
A DWI conviction with a BAC of 0.15 or more, or with another conviction in the past seven years, requires an ignition interlock device on the vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A02
If you are convicted of DWI while already revoked for an earlier DWI, the court may order your vehicle seized and sold. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A03
The legal age to buy any alcoholic beverage in North Carolina is 21, and anyone younger who buys or tries to buy alcohol breaks the law. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A03
An underage person convicted of buying or trying to buy alcohol, or of helping another underage person do so, faces a one-year license revocation. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A03
An underage person convicted of using, or trying to use, a fake license or ID or someone else's license or ID to get alcohol faces a one-year revocation. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A03
Any person convicted of letting an underage person use their license or ID to buy alcohol, or of giving alcohol to an underage person, also faces a one-year revocation. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A03
A driver under 21 convicted of driving with any amount of alcohol or drugs in their body loses their license for one year. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-F32 | anchor: A03
DWI laws can change with new legislation, and updates are posted on the General Assembly website. [A03]
Why it matters: dynamic fact; penalty details should be refreshed from the legislature website.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0035]

Misconceptions: refusing the chemical test does not avoid a penalty, it triggers its own revocation; a driver below the per se limit can still be convicted if impairment is shown; underage drivers face an any-amount rule, not the adult limit; a closed container in a car's passenger area is not the same as an open one, but in a commercial vehicle both are banned.
Mnemonics: two roads to DWI — Impaired or Over the limit; the restoration restriction tightens from a small allowance on the first restoration to none on the next.
Glossary: BAC means blood alcohol concentration; DWI means Driving While Impaired, the single impaired-driving offense; chemical test means a breath or blood test; ignition interlock means a device that blocks starting the vehicle when alcohol is detected; Limited Driving Privilege means court-granted restricted driving during a revocation.
Dynamic facts: DWI penalties can change by legislation and are flagged as dynamic; confirm current law on the General Assembly website.
